practice_name: Site prep — survey, utilities, strip, test hole (SFR)
habit_scope: Survey stakes, utility locate, test hole, strip topsoil, protect trees/buried cables, remove stumps. ORNL SITEWORK; CMHC Ch6 Location and Excavation (Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC); HUD R401.4 soils fork lives in the geotech alts. 1–2 story wood SFR. Not the hole (P04). Not the foundation (P05).
how_it_is_done: Locate stakes and benchmarks (ORNL SITEWORK). CMHC Ch6: after the site is cleared, mark the perimeter of the house using the exact location of the corners of the lot as a reference. 'The latter are usually determined by a certified surveyor, marked by small wooden stakes accurately located at each corner, with nails driven into their tops indicating the outside line of the foundation walls.' Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. CMHC Ch2 Building Layout: 'The services of a land surveyor may be required to establish the distances from the foundation to property lines, locate the municipal services and establish the layout and the depth of the excavation.'

Call utilities before you dig. CMHC Ch6: 'Always check with local utility companies prior to digging to ensure that the excavation will not interfere with buried services. Inadvertently cutting telephone, gas or power lines can prove costly and result in injury.' Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. ORNL SITEWORK: 'Establish limits of excavation and determine trees, roots, buried cables, pipes, sewers, etc., to be protected from damage.'

Call for a test hole — full-depth hole in the proposed foundation location (ORNL SITEWORK). Confirm elevation of the water table (ORNL). HUD §4.3: soil-bearing investigations rarely required for residential construction except when a history of local problems provides evidence of known risks (organic deposits, landfills, expansive soils, and seismic risk). Default soils path is the presumptive table (m-P01-geotech-spt / m-P01-geotech-dcp are the alts when the code requires a report or the site is a known risk).

Strip and stockpile topsoil (ORNL SITEWORK). CMHC Ch6: 'Before excavating begins, topsoil should be stripped and stored for reuse. Some excavated material suitable for backfill may be stored on site and surplus material removed from the site.' Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Define spoil site (ORNL). AF&PA Foundations: compact fill / stripped-root areas before the pour (P04/P05 hold — do not skip the strip).

Remove stumps and grubbing debris from the site (ORNL SITEWORK). Keep excavations clear of chemical contaminants, refuse or degradable matter such as branches, stumps and roots (CMHC Ch6 Sustainable — Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC). Termite: pull roots, stumps, and scrap wood from the foundation area (ORNL termite; also P06).
Protect existing trees and landscaping where possible (CMHC Ch6). Protect drainage ditches and sewers from silt, soil or chemical contamination (CMHC Ch6). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.

Locate the building at the highest point if the site is wet (ORNL SITEWORK). Confirm water table; a water table within ~8 ft of the surface will likely make a basement undesirable (ORNL §1.3) — that is a type veto, not a P01 Method.

Establish elevations of finish grades, drainage swales, catch basins, foundation drain outfalls, property corners (ORNL SITEWORK). Discharge roof drainage away from the foundation (ORNL). Intercepting drains upgrade of the foundation if needed (ORNL) — this is site drainage, not the P05 footing drain.

Materials on site: CMHC Ch2 Protection and Care of Materials — store wood 200 to 250 mm (8 to 10 in.) above the ground on flat supports, covered; deliver just before use. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. AF&PA: store framing ≥6 in off ground under cover. Do not treat lumber storage as a soils Method.
trades: ORNL checklist: grading contractor, construction contractor, landscape contractor for grade definitions — no crew size
CMHC: certified surveyor; local utility companies — no crew size
tools_equipment: Named: survey stakes with nails in the tops (CMHC); test hole (ORNL). Not a SKU list. No crew tools invented.
inspection_hold_points: Utility locate before digging (CMHC Ch6; ORNL buried cables/pipes/sewers). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
Test hole, full depth, in the proposed foundation location (ORNL SITEWORK).
Water table confirmed (ORNL). Within ~8 ft is a basement veto (ORNL §1.3) — type choice, not a skip-inspection.
Topsoil stripped and stockpiled before the hole (ORNL; CMHC Ch6).
Stakes and lot corners from a certified surveyor (CMHC Ch6). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit. Geotech SPT/DCP is the documented alt when IRC R401.4 requires a report or the site is a known risk.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Skipping the utility locate. Treating the test hole as optional on a known-risk site (HUD organic / landfill / expansive / seismic). Inventing a demo Method the books did not print. Mixing this with P04 excavation or P05 footings.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They did — call before you dig, strip the dirt, find the lot corners. What they skip is the test hole and the water table before they pick a basement.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Soils path (presumptive table vs geotech report) is a permit-gate when IRC R401.4 requires a report. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. HUD prints R401.4 and table R401.4.1.
risk_if_swapped_late: Finding bad soils after the hole is open changes footing size or foundation type. Catch with the test hole / geotech before permit.
plain_language_summary: Call the utilities. Get the lot corners from a surveyor. Dig a test hole where the house will sit. Strip the topsoil and pile it. Pull the stumps. If the site is wet, put the house on the high spot. This is not the hole and it is not the foundation.
spanish_summary: Llame a los servicios. Esquinas del lote de un agrimensor. Haga un pozo de prueba donde irá la casa. Retire y apile la tierra vegetal. Saque tocones. Si el lote está mojado, ponga la casa en lo alto. Esto no es el hueco ni la cimentación.
locators: ORNL BFH SITEWORK checklist (printed p 33): buried cables, test hole, strip topsoil, stakes and benchmarks
CMHC Ch6 Marking the Excavation Area (printed p 60): surveyor stakes, utility locate before digging
HUD RSDG §4.3 / IRC R401.4 and table R401.4.1 (printed p 4-9)
confidence_notes: ORNL SITEWORK + CMHC Ch6 + HUD soils fork. Demo of an existing house not a sequence in these books — Gap. Canadian claims labeled. No crew.
remodel_note: Remodel extras (matching, occupied-site, shoring, demo of an existing house) are not a sequence in CMHC/ORNL/HUD/FM — Gap, do not invent remodel-only methods. Essential Guide is framing-only (opened 2026-08-30; silent on site/layout). B&D Room Additions not used as a P00–P06 sequence.

certs: certified surveyor named (CMHC) — not a license number

labor_notes: CMHC names a certified surveyor and local utility companies. ORNL names grading / construction / landscape contractors for grade words. No crew count.
layering: Utility locate → survey stakes / lot corners → test hole → strip topsoil → protect trees/cables → then layout (P03) and the hole (P04).
Site drainage (swales, intercepting drains upgrade, roof water away from the foundation) is P01/P04 — not the P05 footing drain.
code_to_check: HUD prints IRC section R401.4 (when geotech reports are required) and table R401.4.1 (presumptive soil bearing). Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
CMHC setback/side-yard and surveyor practice is Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
time_money: HUD: tests on stronger-than-average soils can justify smaller footings. CMHC: reuse stripped topsoil. No dollars. Do not invent days.

images.caption: CMHC Fig 28: lot/foundation lines, equal diagonals, batter-board saw kerf + taut line + plumb bob. Surveyor nails in corner stakes mark the outside line of the foundation walls (Ch6). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. 3-4-5 numbers on the figure are CMHC metric multiples — do not copy as US habit; US squaring is FM 6-8-10 (P03).

inspector_looks_for: Utility locate done; buried cables, pipes, sewers protected (ORNL SITEWORK; CMHC Ch6).
Test hole called in the proposed foundation location (ORNL).
Topsoil stripped and stockpiled; spoil site defined (ORNL).
Stakes and benchmarks located; lot corners from a surveyor (ORNL; CMHC).
Stumps and grubbing debris off the site (ORNL).
inspector_fails: Digging before a utility locate — CMHC Ch6 names cutting telephone, gas or power lines as costly and injurious. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
common_messups: Inadvertently cutting telephone, gas or power lines (CMHC Ch6). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
Leaving stumps, roots, and scrap wood in the foundation area (ORNL termite / SITEWORK).
do_not_cheap: Test hole in the proposed foundation location (hold).
Strip and stockpile topsoil; do not bury organics under the house (hold + layering).
Surveyor lot corners before you trust the stakes (CMHC). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
smart_save: HUD: soil-bearing tests on stronger-than-average soils can justify smaller footings — that is the geotech alt, not a field guess. No dollars in sources.
CMHC: store stripped topsoil and good excavated material for backfill/landscape so you import less fill. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. No dollars.
Late swap: a late soils surprise (expansive clay, high water table, organic deposits) changes foundation type. Catch with the test hole / geotech before permit.
sop_gap_note: Demo of an existing house is Gap (gap-P01-demo-existing-house). Fastener_schedule [] — survey nails in stake tops are layout, not a structural schedule. walkthroughs [].
